newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank dismisses Bankcoop complaint.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank dismisses Bankcoop complaint.

text.p: Romania's central bank has dismissed allegations of illegal capital participation into private bank Bankcoop, saying a $10 million capital injection by bussinesman George Paunescu was in line with banking laws.
"Our checks have revealed that the money was not drawn from a credit Paunescu might have taken from a bank operating in Romania," a central bank (BNR) statement said on Friday.
Romanian banking laws ban equity acquisitions in banks with money from credits taken from another bank.

Banca de Credit Cooperatist Bankcoop SA president Alexandru Dinulescu asked the BNR last month to investigate Paunescu's aquisition of Banckoop shares, after accusing Paunescu of trying to take control of the bank.
"In the area of banking activity in Romania, the Bankcoop president's allegations are not confirmed," the BNR said.

The BNR's review followed a complaint lodged by the bank's main corporate founders that Paunescu had taken credits from another Romanian bank in order to buy Bankcoop shares in 1995 and that he repaid the credit with Bankcoop loans.
In a tit-for-tat, Paunescu, who holds 44 percent of Bankcoop, rejected the accusations saying they were "an attempt to cover bad management at the bank".
The row sparked queues last month when people rushed to withdraw their money from Bankcoop's branches across Romania, but the panic subsided soon.

Over the past year problems at two private banks -- Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA and Dacia Felix SA -- undermined confidence in the banking sector, which is still dominated by state banks.

In 1995 Bankcoop fought off local market and media speculation alleging problems at the bank. Later that year Paunescu, head of a large media and tourism holding, acquired $10 million worth of Bankcoop shares.
Bankcoop reported an end-1996 provisional balance sheet of 2.1 trillion lei ($346 million), 870 billion lei up from 1995 and a 1996 gross profit of 66 billion ($10.9 million). ($=6,069 lei)
